tasks.title: Email about holiday planning
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Read this email from your English teacher, Mrs. Hill, and the notes you have made.

promptBlocks.subject: Family holiday by train – your ideas
paragraphs: As you know, our class is helping to plan a family holiday by train. We need to decide on the most important thing to think about. Should we focus on keeping the cost low for families, or on making the journey comfortable with enough space for everyone? Which do you think is more important and why?
Also, we need to choose one practical thing to organise. Would you prefer to book seats together in one carriage, or arrange for a stop where families can stretch their legs?
Finally, can you suggest one way to make the train journey fun for children?

promptBlocks.heading: Notes for your reply
listItems: Say which is more important: low cost OR comfort – and explain why.
Choose a practical thing to organise (book seats together OR plan a stop) and give a reason.
Suggest one way to make the journey fun for children.
Ask Mrs. Hill about the date of the holiday.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to Mrs. Hill using all the notes.

tasks.title: Article about train travel
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: You see this notice on a travel website for families.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted!
paragraphs: Travelling by train with your family – what do you think?
Is a train journey a good way for a family to travel on holiday? What is the best thing about it? What can be difficult?
Write an article answering these questions and we will put it on our website!

tasks.title: Story about a train journey
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
"When the train suddenly stopped between stations, everyone in our carriage looked at each other."
